newsitem.title: UK: Flying Colours takes to the skies.
newsitem.headline: Flying Colours takes to the skies.

text.p: Flying Colours, Britain's newest airline, said Thursday, the first of four brand-new aircraft arrived at its base in Manchester.
After certification by the Civil Aviation Authority(CAA), the Boeing 757-200 will make its first commercial flight on March 6, flying holidaymakers to Lanzarote in the Canary Islands.
The three remaining 757's, one of which will be based at London Gatwick, will be delivered and be in service by early May.

Errol Cossey, the airline's chairman, who has more than 30 years experience in leisure aviation and tour operating, said:"The arrival of this aircraft signals the start of our flying operations and we are confident that we will quickly be recognised as a new force in charter operations and the carrier with whom every holidaymaker wants to fly."

Cossey, the founder of both Air Europe and Air 2000, was the first person to create a charter airline equipped with new, modern aircraft and run them at utilisation levels never fore achieved, the statement said.

Geoff Muirhead, Manchester airport's chief executive said: "The airline committed itself to Manchester, already bringing 267 jobs to the region. The start of a new airline at the airport re-emphasises the importance of the second runway development. - Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel:+44 171 542 7706 Fax:5017
